And he proved from what Bach wrote in siman 177; but Magen Avraham wrote before this that his mind on them helps in every case, even if they were not brought until after he finished eating the fruits; also what he wrote to explain Ri — it appears, etc., that the Talmud in one who eats fruits of Ginosar — and this is his language: that the fruits of Ginosar are very sweet and are not eaten except with much salt so the sweetness not harm him, and they eat them with bread — and bread is found secondary to the fruits; therefore he blesses on the fruits and exempts the bread — end of his words; and Bach holds that Ri explains that the answer remained in the challenger's view that there is nothing where bread is secondary except fruits of Ginosar which are very important relative to them — bread is secondary if he will need afterward to eat salted fish with bread; but relative to salted fish, bread is not secondary.

Therefore they wrote that he blesses on the fruits and exempts the fish and also the bread; and that which the mishnah teaches "he blesses on the salted item" — meaning he blesses on the thing brought on its account, the salted item — namely on the fruits; and so it appears from Rashi there. And he wrote: therefore one should be careful to bring before him fish and bread (namely per his method above that they must be before him) at the time of eating fruits and intend to exempt them by the blessing on the fruits; but if they are not exempted by the blessing on the fruits — whether salted fish exempts bread, this law is in dispute between Tosafot and Ri as above. But Magen Avraham holds that for the law there is no dispute between Tosafot and Ri; Ri also agrees that even if he blesses on salted fish he exempts bread which is secondary relative to fish in such a case where he ate sweet fruits first — only Ri settles Tosafot's difficulty above that he should bless on the fruits, etc.; and for this Ri wrote that in truth such is the mishnah's intent and it does not discuss at all one who eats salted fish, only that he salts the fruits themselves and eats bread with them — then he blesses on the salted item, namely the salted fruits, and exempts the bread.

And Shelah wrote, etc. And it is as if his mind was on it; and otherwise he must bless — and this is Shelah's language: but, etc., and also his mind was not, etc., and also his way is not, etc. — certainly he blesses HaMotzi when they bring him, etc., end of his words; and this — that he blesses HaMotzi and not shehakol — is not like the emendation of Netiv Chayim who emended and placed here what Magen Avraham wrote in this sk 7 "and if his mind was not on it he blesses shehakol on the bread," etc. And otherwise it is impossible to emend thus, and it is easily understood; and Magen Avraham's words in this sk 7 will be explained there, with God's help.

And this is Baal HaMaor regarding, etc. For he explains that which Rif on daf 41b taught: things that come because of the meal within the meal do not require a blessing before them or after them, as Rashi there — that they come to dip the bread and he dips in them; and therefore bread exempts them, for the primary exempts the secondary (and we do not hold thus except like Tosafot and as above siman 177) — for otherwise Rif would have to say, etc. Meaning: he is the teacher of the halachah of things that come because of the meal, etc., and he wanted to say: since it did not come to teach us that bread exempts, since it is primary — for this is explained in the mishnah — rather it came to innovate that even if his mind was not on it, why was it necessary to establish a separate statement? He should have placed his words on the mishnah that teaches "the primary exempts the secondary" — Rif should have said: and even if his mind was not on it.

And if his mind was not on it he blesses shehakol on the bread, as written in the gloss — and certainly it is impossible to say that this refers to what is adjacent above, for if so there is no understanding of Magen Avraham's words; rather he returns to the earlier ones to dispute Bach; and what he wrote in between — Shelah's words and Baal HaMaor's — are like a gloss as if it is enclosed in two half-circles, as is his way in many places; and his intent is that above he disputed Bach who holds that if fish and bread were not exempted by the blessing on the fruits, bread is not exempted by shehakol that one blesses on the fish, but rather he must bless on the bread HaMotzi per Ri's view — and if so in this case it is the dispute of Tosafot and Ri as above. But per Magen Avraham's explanation of Ri as above, for the law Ri agrees that even if his mind was not at the time of blessing on the fruits on the fish and bread — nevertheless bread is called secondary relative to salted fish; and if so bread is exempted by shehakol which is the blessing of salted fish. And even if he eats bread before salted fish — since bread is secondary, he blesses on the bread shehakol as the blessing of salted fish, as Rama wrote in the gloss. And in this case where the primary's blessing is shehakol, Magen Avraham agrees in sk 4 to Rama's gloss — see there.

magen_avraham.he:
שאין מתכונין. אבל במדינות אלו שמניחין המרקחת על הדובשנין שטובים למאכל א"כ כונתו ג"כ לאכילת הדובשנים ומברך עליהם:
לאכול לחם. רק שבאים לדבק המרקחת עליה' שלא יטנפו הידים בדבש:
magen_avraham.en:
That one does not intend. But in these countries they place the spread on honey cakes that are fit for food — if so, his intent is also for eating the honey cakes and he blesses on them.

To eat bread. Only that they come to attach the spread to them so the hands are not soiled with honey.

mishnah_berurah.he:
(יב) הוו טפילה למרקחת - וצריך לברך על המרקחת לבד:
(יג) לאכול לחם - רק שבאים לדבק המרקחת עליהם שלא יטנפו הידים בדבש ועיין באחרונים שכתבו דבמדינותינו שעושין הדובשנין שטובים למאכל ומניחין המרקחת עליהם א"כ כונתו ג"כ לאכילת הדובשנין ומברך עליהם ועיין לעיל סימן קס"ח במ"ב סקמ"ה שמבואר שם כל פרטי דין זה:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(12) They are secondary to the paste — and he must bless on the paste alone.
(13) To eat bread — only that they come to attach the spread to them so the hands are not soiled with honey; and see in the acharonim who wrote that in our countries they make honey cakes that are fit for food and place the spread on them — if so, his intent is also for eating the honey cakes and he blesses on them; and see above siman 168 in Mishna Berurah sk 45 where all details of this law are explained.

peri_megadim.he: כדי עט״ז בגמרא ומי איכא מידי כו׳ ופי׳ רש״י ים כנרת חשובים מפת ובר״מ פ״ג מה״ב ה״ז הרי שצריך לאכול מליח עב״ח ובפי׳ המשנה אינה אלא בשומרי גנות ומשמע ל״ד פירות גינוסר אלא כל שאכל מתיקה וצריך למלוח לחתך הליחות הנדבקות באצטומכא אבל הטור והמחבר כתבו אפי׳ דג מליח לחוד. ולהרר״י באמת י״ל זה מי איכא מידי דפת טפילה לפירות והפירות הם ללפת כו׳ ועתי״ט:
peri_megadim.en: So that. Taz: in the Gemara "and is there anything," etc.; and Rashi explained: Sea of Kinneret fruits are more important than bread; and Rambam chapter 3 of Blessings halachah 7 — behold one must eat salty food because of them; and in explanation of the mishnah it is only regarding garden guards; and it implies to some fruits of Ginosar only — but all who ate sweetness and needs salty food to cut the sweetness sticking in the esophagus; but Tur and Mechaber wrote even salted fish alone. And for Rashal — in truth one may say: is there anything where bread is secondary to fruits and the fruits are relish, etc.; and it requires study.

turei_zahav.he: רקיקים הוו טפל' למרקחת נראה דזה דוקא אם אוכל הרקיקין עם המרקחת אבל אם אכל המרקחת מלמעל' והשאיר הרקיקין ואוכלן בפ"ע צריכין ברכה הראויי' להם דאז עשה מהם ג"כ עיקר:
turei_zahav.en: The crackers are secondary to the paste — it appears this is specifically if he eats the crackers with the paste; but if he ate the paste from above and left the crackers and eats them by themselves — they require their proper blessing, for then he has made them primary as well.
